prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Finished individual portrait for the ARC Daily Card Cabinet in the editor-approved 1950s pulp science-fiction / retro space-western direction. Authentic confident black brush outlines, painted gouache shading, fine four-color halftone and warm paper grain; vigorous saturated printed color. Every face, hand, cable and machine is drawn in ONE coherent medium. Adult naturally proportioned human features, normal-sized eyes, strong mid-century painted facial planes. NO anime, manga, chibi, giant eyes, baby face, photographic skin or photo-head collage. Source cartoon avatars establish character motifs, not verified owner human likenesses. Preserve recognizable chosen character cues while converting the illustration language. Ingenious, lightly ridiculous outsized graphics-card equipment and visible colored square ARC puzzle screens. Facial equipment physically attaches at temples/ears/cheeks with visible cabling routed into the collar and compute rig. All hardware has believable brackets, harness and weight. No scarf, cape, identical twin-GPU pillars, matching bubble-helmet uniform, medieval fantasy armor or generic neon cyber suit. Full-bleed PORTRAIT5:7, ideally1500x2100, head-through-hips; all essential headgear, hands and unique apparatus contained. Face near upper third, calmer dark lower edge usable for later overlays. NO words, letters, digits, logos, titles, speech balloons, captions, watermark, card frame or border. ONE main person only. Input1 is Lukas's chosen individual avatar. Input2 is his established team character sheet: use ONLY the LEFTMOST navy/blue dancer for wardrobe and gestures, no other teammates. Input3 supplies vintage pulp art technique and adult male facial construction, not a face to copy. Preserve swept chestnut quiff, clean-shaven face, blue-gray eyes, friendly confident expression and blue/navy ARC-grid costume. Portray an original adult male frontier rocket courier with the theatrical swagger of a dance-floor ace, mature cheekbones and normally sized eyes. Torso in a lively twisting three-quarter pose, one hand adjusting a big lever on his unusual rig, other making a relaxed open-palmed expressive gesture. No claim about actual occupation or skills.
Distinct equipment design: a huge PORTABLE COMPUTE JUKEBOX slung diagonally across lower torso on a broad worn brown leather pilot harness, approximately chest-wide, one recognizable long green graphics-card board inside a riveted polished aluminum chassis, TWO enormous cooling fans arranged HORIZONTALLY across its front, deep copper heatsink fins, exposed valve tubes at one end, large tactile rotary controls and bright small multicolored ARC tile windows. A single swept rocket-style fin and corrugated exhaust hose rise behind one shoulder; one wrist carries a chunky square mechanical puzzle controller. It reads as a ridiculous wearable graphics-card instrument, not the twin upright fan towers from earlier portraits. Navy and cobalt leather flight jacket with multicolored square ARC patchwork panels echoes the exact established dancer costume; cream ribbing and brushed aluminum, small red-orange accents. Headgear: a slim yet mechanically substantial silver half-headset with copper ear receiver, articulated transparent amber scan lens over only one eye, visible bolted temple hinge, cheek pickup and coiled wires into collar; hair and expression exposed. Atmospheric rocket-depot scoring hall with chrome jukebox-like consoles, geometric ARC grid dance-floor reflected in background and an orange desert horizon. Strong playful pulp adventure energy, distinct from a radio operator and from a space queen. Do not reproduce incidental writing on his original hoodie.
